frozen_original.title: Trump Calls for Termination of the Constitution
frozen_original.synopsis: On December 3, 2022, Trump posted on Truth Social calling for the 'termination of all rules, regulations, articles, even those found in the Constitution' in order to reinstate him as president and nullify the 2020 election. The statement was widely condemned by constitutional scholars, Democrats, and even some Republicans as the most explicit anti-democratic statement a former president had ever made. Trump's own vice president Mike Pence said the remarks were 'wrong' and called on Trump to apologize. The episode was cited by January 6 Committee members as further evidence of Trump's contempt for constitutional governance. No significant disciplinary action or legal consequence followed.

frozen_original.title: Trump Ends DACA — 700,000 Dreamers Face Deportation
frozen_original.synopsis: On September 5, 2017, Attorney General Jeff Sessions announced the end of Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA), the Obama-era program protecting approximately 700,000 young immigrants who had grown up in the United States from deportation. Sessions falsely claimed DACA was unconstitutional, though it had withstood legal scrutiny for years. The termination gave Congress six months to act, but no legislative replacement was passed. Federal courts repeatedly blocked the full dismantling of DACA. The Supreme Court ruled in Department of Homeland Security v. Regents of the University of California (2020) that the rescission was 'arbitrary and capricious.' The decision left hundreds of thousands of young people who had known no other country in prolonged legal limbo.

frozen_original.title: Trump Administration Ends Export Control Enforcement, Enabling Tech Transfers to Adversaries
frozen_original.synopsis: In 2025, the Trump administration dismantled key portions of the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) export control enforcement infrastructure, firing enforcement staff and halting prosecution of cases involving illegal technology transfers to China, Russia, and Iran. Export controls prevent adversary nations from acquiring advanced US technology — particularly semiconductors, AI systems, and dual-use equipment — for military and intelligence applications. Former BIS officials described the enforcement collapse as a strategic gift to China's military modernization program and Russia's sanctions-evasion efforts. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick characterized export controls as bureaucratic impediments to business, signaling that enforcement would not be a priority. Intelligence officials warned the decision would accelerate adversary weapons development programs that US export controls had been designed to retard.
